\subsubsection{Power and Corners}\label{sss:pixtop-power}

One channel draws \SI{1.642}{\milli\watt} at the nominal process point,
\SI{656.55}{\micro\ampere} from the \SI{2.5}{\volt} analog rail and
\SI{1.04}{\micro\ampere} from the \SI{1.0}{\volt} converter core, against a
\SI{1}{\milli\watt} target. Over the four process corners the analog rail spans
\SIrange{517}{1075}{\micro\ampere}, so the fast corner misses the
\SI{400}{\micro\ampere} rail budget by \(2.7\times\).

\SI{806.8}{\micro\watt} of that --- more than half of the
\SI{1.455}{\milli\watt} that rolls up per block --- is the two reference-DAC
supply regulators, whose outputs reach nothing (Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-open}).
The figure above is measured with them present. Deleting them is measured to
change nothing else: every dc quantity in Table~\ref{tab:pixtop-summary} is
bit-identical over all 32 swept potential codes, and the channel falls to
\SI{836}{\micro\watt}. They cannot simply be turned off, because one enable pin
drives both a ladder and its regulator and pulling it low collapses the common
mode; removing them is a schematic change. The rest of the rollup is the two
amplifiers at \SI{487.5}{\micro\watt}, the local bias generator at
\SI{59.3}{\micro\watt}, the two ladders at \SI{88.8}{\micro\watt} and the
converter at \SI{12.3}{\micro\watt}. The rollup does not close against the
\SI{1.642}{\milli\watt} the rails deliver, because it does not follow the
inherited supply ports; the rail figure is the authoritative one.

All twenty dc-reachable specs --- reference tracking, the potential range, the
common mode, the zero-current offsets and the gain-code sweep --- pass at all
five corners. That is weaker evidence than it looks: the corner rows keep the
resistor and capacitor models typical, so for a block whose accuracy is set by
matching they exercise almost nothing. Monte Carlo is the real test, and
Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-mc} puts uncalibrated per-channel yield at
\SI{0.50}{\percent} on the same specifications these corners all pass.
